stories.title: Deloitte reports corporate sustainability entering a disciplined phase
stories.summary: Deloitte Global's 2026 survey of 2,100 C-suite leaders suggests corporate sustainability has moved from broad ambition to focused execution. The report highlights a shift toward ROI, resilience, and technology as enablers. Sustainability remains a top priority, though the focus is now on disciplined, measurable business value.

stories.title: Investors flag gaps in sustainability reporting standards
stories.summary: Pension-linked investors have backed the International Sustainability Standards Board's efforts to improve disclosures while noting shortcomings. Concerns include inconsistent measurement, weak links to financial risk, and gaps in workforce reporting. The board is currently reviewing industry-specific standards across two rounds of consultation.

stories.title: EU agrees on new ESG investment categories
stories.summary: EU co-legislators have reached an agreement on three new investment product categories. Under the new framework, fossil fuel firms are permitted in some ESG funds. The Council of the European Union confirmed the agreement, which establishes distinct categories for sustainable investment products.

stories.title: Investors support ISSB review of sustainability disclosures
stories.summary: Major pension-linked investors are backing the International Sustainability Standards Board's review of industry-specific sustainability disclosures. The board is currently consulting on comprehensive amendments to nine standards and targeted changes to 41 others. Investors are using these disclosures to assess financial risk.

stories.title: European Commission consults on sustainability reporting assurance
stories.summary: The European Commission has launched a consultation on standards for limited assurance of sustainability reporting under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive. The standards will be based on technical advice from the Committee of European Auditing Oversight Bodies, adapted to reflect the EU legal framework.

stories.title: Wipro files annual sustainability report
stories.summary: Wipro Limited has filed its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for the 2025-26 financial year. The company reports a 92 percent reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions and 94 percent renewable energy sourcing. The filing received reasonable assurance from Deloitte Haskins and Sells LLP.

stories.title: KPMG survey shows Indian CEOs remain confident in growth
stories.summary: The KPMG 2026 India CEO Outlook suggests leaders remain confident despite economic and geopolitical volatility. CEOs are prioritizing resilience by increasing investments in cybersecurity, digital capabilities, and workforce development. Sustainability remains a key priority as firms look to turn resilience into long-term growth.

stories.title: EHS teams may be better prepared for CSRD reporting
stories.summary: Environmental, health, and safety professionals may find the European Union's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive less daunting than expected. Much of the required data, including waste records and safety metrics, is already collected through everyday EHS activities. The challenge lies in integrating this information into broader reporting.

stories.title: Group-IB publishes 2025 sustainability report
stories.summary: Group-IB has released its 2025 sustainability report, detailing its work against digital crime alongside ESG progress. The company contributed to six international operations, resulting in 1,809 arrests and the dismantling of 34,838 pieces of malicious infrastructure. Adversary-centric intelligence remains the company's primary operational focus.

stories.title: Quess Corp CDP rating improves
stories.summary: Quess Corp Limited announced its Carbon Disclosure Project rating for climate change improved from C to B for the 2026 assessment year. The company attributed the upgrade to strengthened environmental management. CDP is a non-profit that runs an environmental disclosure platform for companies worldwide.

stories.title: A. O. Smith releases 2026 sustainability report
stories.summary: A. O. Smith Corporation has published its 2026 sustainability report, covering performance from 2025 and 2026. The company states it exceeded its environmental goals for greenhouse gas emissions intensity, operational water savings, and landfill waste reduction. This is the company's fifth report in eight years.

NK Singh urges aggressive use of multilateral balance sheets
stories.summary: At COP31, NK Singh argued that climate financing gaps could be narrowed by using the balance sheets of multilateral development banks more aggressively. He framed the global agenda around mobilizing finance, managing the shift to renewable fuels, and building carbon markets to meet climate goals.

stories.title: Ottawa selects 19 carbon removal projects for credit purchase
stories.summary: The federal government has selected 19 carbon dioxide removal projects from which departments can purchase credits to offset emissions. The government established competitive standing offers for these credits, describing the move as a first among national governments. The projects include 18 private firms and one First Nation.

stories.title: Uganda launches national carbon project register
stories.summary: Uganda has launched the National Carbon Project Register at COP31. The system, titled One Ledger of Trust, provides a single record of all carbon market activity within the country. It covers the entire lifecycle of carbon credits, from project approval to final use.

stories.title: Singapore expands carbon market agreements at COP31
stories.summary: Singapore has signed carbon credit implementation agreements with Kenya and Zambia, bringing its total to 14 bilateral deals. The frameworks support Article 6 carbon credit transfers and climate adaptation. A separate memorandum of understanding with Bangladesh was also signed to explore future cooperation.

stories.title: Singapore and Zambia sign carbon credit agreement
stories.summary: Singapore and Zambia have signed a legally binding implementation agreement for carbon credit collaboration under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The framework allows project developers to generate and transfer credits aligned with international rules. Eligible methodologies and authorization processes are included in the agreement.

stories.title: Uzbekistan explores carbon market deals at COP31
stories.summary: Uzbekistan's state mining companies have signed memorandums with UK-based Valor Carbon to explore carbon market opportunities. The country is seeking international financing for nearly 20 environmental projects. No specific financial commitments or projects have been announced following the signings at COP31.

stories.title: Ghana receives first African ART TREES carbon credits
stories.summary: Ghana has been issued 6.57 million carbon credits under the Architecture for REDD+ Transactions programme, the first African nation to do so. The government expects to generate US$43 million from the sale of credits covering forest protection efforts between 2017 and 2021. The forest remains intact.

stories.title: Guinea plans forest carbon credit launch for 2027
stories.summary: Guinea aims to issue its first high-integrity forest carbon credits by 2027. Minister Fassou Théa announced the strategy during COP31, citing support from the United Kingdom and the World Bank to strengthen institutional capacity for managing natural resources. The country is currently preparing its forest heritage for valuation.

stories.title: IEEFA suggests insurers fund India's renewable transition
stories.summary: A report by the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis suggests that allocating 1% of life insurance assets could unlock INR 68,000 crore for India's renewable energy sector. Domestic insurers currently favor listed companies, while foreign investors provide most growth equity for unlisted firms. Capital is waiting.

stories.title: Canadian government to purchase carbon credits for departments
stories.summary: The federal government is set to buy carbon credits to offset emissions from departments it describes as hard to decarbonize, including defence. The government has selected 19 projects, many involving carbon capture and storage technology. The government is now a customer of its own climate policy.

stories.title: COP31 hosts indoor butterfly conservatory
stories.summary: Delegates at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya are sharing space with 20,000 tropical butterflies in a 2,600 square meter conservatory. The indoor garden maintains a steady 28 degrees Celsius and 80 percent humidity. The insects are currently the only residents meeting their climate targets.

stories.title: European Commission signs 25 million euro loss and damage agreement
stories.summary: The European Commission has signed a 25 million euro contribution agreement for the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage. The funding formalizes a pledge made at COP28 as the fund shifts toward active operations. The money is intended to support vulnerable countries facing climate change impacts.

stories.title: COP31 draft removes fossil fuel references
stories.summary: The latest draft of the COP31 climate summit outcome has removed all mentions of fossil fuels. Campaigners have labeled the event a ghost summit, as parallel texts also failed to clarify financial support for developing nations. The negotiations are currently approaching their final hours.

stories.title: Fossil fuel language absent from COP31 draft
stories.summary: Explicit references to transitioning away from coal, oil and gas have been removed from the latest draft climate agreement at COP31. While the text acknowledges the 1.5 degree Celsius goal, it drops specific roadmaps for fossil fuel reduction. Ambition remains a point of discussion.

stories.title: COP31 draft agreement sparks criticism
stories.summary: A revised draft agreement at the COP31 summit in Turkey has removed all references to fossil fuels. The change has prompted anger from environmental groups as the nearly 200 participating countries face a Friday deadline. The summit continues amid a record-breaking El Niño.

COP31 negotiators publish fossil-fuel-free draft
stories.summary: Climate negotiators have removed all references to ending fossil fuel use from the latest draft deal at the COP31 summit. The document encourages the deployment of technologies to suck carbon out of the air. The Friday deadline for a final agreement is approaching.

stories.title: COP31 draft proposes increased adaptation finance
stories.summary: The latest COP31 draft cover decision proposes tripling adaptation finance by 2035 and accelerating electrification. The nine-page document removes previous language regarding a transition away from fossil fuels. Contentious issues remain unresolved as the summit nears its conclusion.

stories.title: Advocates criticize COP31 draft text
stories.summary: The latest COP31 draft cover decision has been described by Oil Change International as a fossil fuel executive's dream. The text removes all references to transitioning away from fossil fuels while setting a goal for electricity to reach 35 percent of global final energy consumption by 2035.

stories.title: Panama threatens to block COP31 agreement
stories.summary: Panama has threatened to block the final COP31 agreement unless it includes a clear path to transition away from fossil fuels. The country is advocating for a cap on oil production as a verifiable step. The summit is currently testing the limits of incremental progress.

stories.title: COP31 draft faces backlash over missing commitments
stories.summary: Civil society organizations have criticized the latest COP31 draft for removing fossil fuel commitments and failing to provide concrete climate finance. The second draft, released on November 19, drops roadmaps for moving away from fossil fuels that appeared in earlier versions. The talks are nearing their end.

stories.title: COP31 draft emphasizes carbon capture over phaseout
stories.summary: The latest COP31 draft text has dropped language regarding a fossil fuel phaseout in favor of an emphasis on carbon capture and storage. Activists have criticized the reliance on technologies that are not yet deployed at scale. The summit is currently debating its final commitments.

stories.title: Audi establishes circular economy business unit
stories.summary: Audi is launching Audi Circular Solutions GmbH in early 2027 to manage vehicle dismantling and parts recycling. The company aims to turn the circular economy into a business model by selling used parts and recovering raw materials. The car has been asked to live forever.

stories.title: Audi Circular Solutions GmbH Makes The Circular Economy A Business Model
stories.summary: Audi is establishing Audi Circular Solutions GmbH to develop a profitable business model around vehicle dismantling, used-parts sales and recycled material recovery. Beginning operations in early 2027, the subsidiary will work with European recycling partners to expand parts reuse, secure secondary raw materials and reduce dependence on virgin resources, with

stories.summary: German automaker Audi has established Audi Circular Solutions GmbH, a wholly owned subsidiary to convert end-of-life vehicle parts into a scalable business model. Slated to begin operations in early 2027, the new division will focus on reusing vehicle parts, dismantling retired cars, and securing secondary raw materials to strengthen supply

stories.title: MMCM issues world’s first carbon credits from vehicle recycling
stories.summary: Meta Materials Circular Markets has issued 24,988 carbon credits for recycling end-of-life vehicles across 20 Indian facilities. The platform developed a method to measure emissions avoided by recovering materials instead of producing new ones. The credits were announced at COP31 in Turkey.

stories.title: UNDP and NPAP discuss Ghana plastics treaty
stories.summary: The United Nations Development Programme and the Ghana National Plastic Action Partnership held a dialogue on national preparations for a global plastics treaty. The project is funded by a 7 million dollar grant from the Global Environment Facility to promote circularity in the plastics sector.

stories.title: BCG report highlights circular economy mineral value
stories.summary: BCG analysis suggests circular economy models could double the gross value added of the German sector to 130 billion euros by 2045. The firm argues that reusing materials is vital as demand for critical minerals is projected to outpace supply through 2040.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu releases warehousing and circular economy policies
stories.summary: Chief Minister M.K. Stalin has released the Tamil Nadu Warehousing Policy 2026 and the Circular Economy Investment Policy 2026. The warehousing framework offers a 25 percent fixed capital subsidy for logistics projects and provides additional concessions for green infrastructure in industrially underdeveloped districts.

stories.title: RESITES: Recovery of recycled fibres into composites | Tecnalia
stories.summary: Composite materials reinforced with carbon fibre and glass fibre are widely used in strategic industrial sectors due to their light weight and high performance. However, their manufacture and end-of-life disposal generate significant volumes of waste, the recovery of which continues to be a technological and industrial challenge. RESITES tackles this

stories.title: Pandrol receives circular economy award from SNCF
stories.summary: Pandrol has been recognised by France’s national railway company SNCF for its circular economy leadership. The award specifically highlights the company's work on under sleeper pads and its commitment to keeping materials in use within the rail network.

stories.title: Amazon targets 65 percent cut in electricity emissions intensity
stories.summary: Amazon plans to reduce the carbon intensity of its global electricity use by 65 percent by 2030 and invest 7 billion dollars in Indian renewable energy. The company's total carbon footprint rose in 2025, with emissions from purchased electricity increasing by more than a third.

stories.summary: New India commitment: Amazon plans to invest $7 billion in Indian renewables by 2030. - Four new projects: Wind and solar deals totaling 934 MW span three Indian states. - Carbon intensity goal: Amazon aims to cut its electricity’s carbon intensity by 65% by 2030. stories.title: KKR acquires minority stake in Gentari India
stories.summary: KKR has acquired a minority stake in Gentari Renewables India, a subsidiary of the clean energy provider launched by Petronas. The platform currently holds approximately 8 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity. Gentari will retain strategic oversight and operational control of the business.

Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal as emissions rise 45 percent
stories.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero target after reporting a 45 percent increase in greenhouse gas emissions last year. Executives cited the infrastructure demands of artificial intelligence as the primary cause for the rising figures. The company has not yet announced a new timeline for its climate goals.

stories.title: Meta puts 2030 net-zero pledge under review as AI emissions jump 45 percent
stories.summary: Meta is reconsidering the 2030 net-zero deadline it set in 2020, citing the infrastructure required to run artificial intelligence. The company reported that emissions rose to 11.8 million metric tons in 2025. The sustainability report confirms that the target is now harder to hit than previously anticipated.

stories.title: Meta says re-evaluating 2030 net-zero target amid AI buildout
stories.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero goal as emissions increased 45 percent to 11.8 million metric tons in 2025. The company stated that growth in the artificial intelligence industry has outpaced efficiency gains. The commitment to the original timeline is currently under review.

research.title: Antarctica’s ice cliffs are collapsing faster than expected, but there’s a twist
research.summary: A surprising new study suggests Antarctica's towering ice cliffs may be less vulnerable to catastrophic collapse than scientists once feared. After tracking more than 15,000 ice cliffs, researchers discovered that even the tallest cliffs, which can collapse at alarming speeds, often stabilize rather than triggering an unstoppable chain.

research.title: Projection of global daily CO2 emissions in 2026
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Global fossil-fuel combustion and industrial-process CO2 emissions remain close to historical highs, yet the recent slowdown in growth is difficult to assess before conventional inventories become available. We project emissions for 2026 and examine daily departures. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
